strategies.name: vwap_trend_continuation_reclaim
strategies.entry_summary: In a directional session where the trader already has a bullish or bearish idea, wait for price to extend away from VWAP into at least the first, preferably the second, standard-deviation band, then enter in the trend direction after price breaks back through and retests that band/reclaim level.
strategies.exit_summary: Use the outer VWAP bands as profit targets, specifically the second and third standard deviations; no other stop mechanic is stated.

variants.variant_label: Long continuation after reclaim from lower value area
variants.timeframe_note: intraday session / New York session examples
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for price to travel to the first or second deviation, then break and test the level before entering long
variants.target_note: use second and third standard deviations as targets
variants.transcript_quote: you might want to wait until the price has gone at least to the first if not the second standard deviation... and after we broke it and tested it weu0

strategies.name: vwap_band_mean_reversion
strategies.entry_summary: Use the outer VWAP standard-deviation bands as overbought/oversold levels for reversal trades: when price reaches the outer premium or discount bands, look for a reversal entry expecting rebalancing back toward fair value.
strategies.exit_summary: Target the central VWAP as the price-rebalancing objective. No concrete stop-loss rule is taught.

variants.variant_label: Reversal from premium or discount outer bands back to VWAP
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: treat outer standard deviations as overbought/oversold areas for reversal setups
variants.transcript_quote: if you're using reversal strategies you might want to use these as some sort of overbought or oversold levels... and use the central vwap as a target

result.enumeration_note: The video teaches two opposed executable skeletons using VWAP bands: continuation after reclaim in a directional context, and mean-reversion from outer bands back to VWAP. Stops are not concretely specified for either, but the exits taught are target-based.
